AISC 1000.title: Foundations of AI Literacy: Human-AI Orchestration
AISC 1000.description: Foundations of AI Literacy: Human-AI Orchestration is a course for first-year undergraduate students that equips them with the cognitive, technical, and ethical foundations to operate effectively in human-AI ecosystems. The course develops AI literacy as orchestration: understanding AI systems from tools to agents; understanding human cognition (attention, memory, bias, metacognition); and designing workflows that treat AI as a collaborator rather than a shortcut. Students’ progress from individual AI collaboration to team orchestration and then to organizational and societal governance, equity, and human flourishing, using interactive activities and real-world cases to support longitudinal integration rather than isolated topic coverage. Graded DI/PA/F.
cilos: Explain core AI concepts and system types (data, training/inference, LLMs, agentic systems) and how these shape capabilities, limits, and failure modes
Apply cognitive and metacognitive concepts (cognitive load/offloading, bias, calibration) to improve learning and decision-making when working with AI
Design human–AI workflows for learning, creativity, and problem-solving that include validation, documentation, and appropriate delegation (AI as partner, not shortcut)
Analyze human–AI work as interconnected knowledge systems across scales (individual, team, organization, society), identifying coordination challenges, cascading risks, and appropriate controls
Evaluate ethical, governance, and equity implications of AI use and justify responsible choices that support human wellbeing and flourishing

AISC 2500.title: Special Topics (I)
AISC 2500.description: This special topics course will help students to gain a better understanding on the topics related to their interdisciplinary studies. A range of professional activities are eligible for study, including seminars/ lectures, professional activities/ meetings, journal readings or structured readings. May be repeated for credits if different topics are taken. May be graded by letter, P/F or DI/PA/F for different offerings.
cilos: Equip with broad and useful knowledge to various topics which are not covered by existing courses.
(Each offering under the umbrella will have specific learning outcomes.)

AISC 2800.title: AIS Cooperative Education Program
AISC 2800.description: This course is intended to enhance AIS students’ career readiness by combining classroom-based education with practical work experience. By taking any two standalone career development programs offered by the Career Center or those as recognized by the School, students are required to apply the skills and knowledge learnt in a full-time coop work experience for a single employer for at least 4 months. Approval from the course coordinator is required for enrollment in the course. For AIS Year 2 students or above only. Graded P, PP or F.
cilos: Apply academic knowledge and/or transferable skills to real-life situations.
Learn and demonstrate the practical application of career skills in real-world scenarios within the chosen industry.
Cultivate effective communication, teamwork, and critical thinking abilities through hands-on experiences in diverse workplace settings.
Strengthen employability through gaining industry-specific experience and mastering workplace dynamics for seamless career transitions.
Build valuable connections with industry experts and peers to unlock potential career pathways.

AISC 4950.title: Interdisciplinary Special Project
AISC 4950.description: Special projects on selected interdisciplinary topics supervised by one or a group of faculty members. May be repeated for credits if different topics are taken. Enrollment may require approval of the course instructor. For DDP, RMBI, EVMT, and IIM students or those with approval from instructor for enrolling in the course. May be graded by letter, P/F or DI/PA/F for different offerings.
cilos: Enhance understanding on selected interdisciplinary topics and real world issues, such as Technology, Entrepreneurship, Business and Sustainability.
Acquire updated market knowledge and skills through the interactions with instructors/ guest speakers from industry professions.
Develop multi-dimensional perspectives and interdisciplinary problem-solving skills that allow them to tackle cross-cultural and multi-faceted issues with a holistic approach.
Develop the potential to be caring leaders of society.

AISC 6500.title: Special Topics for Interdisciplinary Studies
AISC 6500.description: This course covers selected topics of current interest in emerging interdisciplinary areas which are not covered in the present curriculum. May be repeated for credit if different topics are covered. May be graded by letter, P/F for different offerings.
cilos: Communicate complex ideas related to interdisciplinary topic in professional and other settings.
Explain the core ideas and concepts of impacts in the topic concerned.
Relate the concepts and methodologies in the course topic to practical implementation.

AISC 6770.title: Professional Development for Interdisciplinary Programs
AISC 6770.description: This one-credit course aims at providing research postgraduate students basic training in ethics, teaching skills, research management, career development, and related professional skills. This course consists of a number of mini-workshops. Graded PP, P or F.

AISC 6950.title: Interdisciplinary Project
AISC 6950.description: An independent project on selected interdisciplinary topics carried out under the supervision of a faculty member. The course may be repeated once for credit. Enrollment requires approval of course instructor. Maybe graded by letter, P/F for different offerings.
cilos: Develop and apply self-learning and task management skills to effectively manage an independent project on a specific interdisciplinary topic.
Critically analyze a selected topic to identify, formulate and solve problems and apply solutions to practical implementations.
Apply the interdisciplinary approach in reviewing the latest developments, technologies or management strategies of the chosen topic.
Communicate effectively in writing, using accurate technical and scientific terminology, and demonstrating logical organization of relevant content and information.
